title: Daily Bread
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
At a private Christian law-school coffee night, Lydia, an undercover police detective, told Barnabas, a local drug dealer, that she wanted to buy cocaine but needed time to raise the necessary funds. Barnabas said that he needed time to get the cocaine. They agreed to meet again in 10 days outside the Daily Bread coffee shop. An hour later, without a warrant, other officers forcibly entered Barnabas’s apartment and arrested him for attempted possession of a controlled substance.

If Barnabas is prosecuted in a common law jurisdiction for attempted possession of cocaine, should he be convicted?
call: If Barnabas is prosecuted in a common law jurisdiction for attempted possession of cocaine, should he be convicted?

choices.A: No, because he had not taken sufficient steps toward commission of the crime.
choices.B: No, because he was illegally arrested.
choices.C: Yes, because by objective standards Lydia and Barnabas had made an agreement that Barnabas would obtain cocaine.
choices.D: Yes, because he unequivocally expressed his intent to obtain the cocaine.

rightExplanation:
A is correct. The call asks whether Barnabas can be convicted of attempted possession. He only talked, agreed to meet later, and said he needed time to get the cocaine. The answer that matches the call is the one focused on the missing step toward the crime.

Gold Key: Attempt is not just criminal desire, talk, or agreement. The defendant must take conduct beyond preparation toward the target crime.

Silver Key: Sort the answers by what they prove: arrest problem, agreement, intent, or act step. On an attempt call, the act-step answer controls.

wrongExplanations.B:
The warrantless entry is an arrest/search problem. The call is conviction for attempted possession. That is an adjacent-call trap.
Silver Key: If the answer talks about the arrest, but the call asks whether the defendant committed attempt, it is answering the wrong link in the chain.
wrongExplanations.C:
It proves an agreement. Agreement language points toward a different inchoate-crime frame. The call is attempt.
Gold Key: Attempt needs a step toward the crime; agreement alone does not make an attempt.
wrongExplanations.D:
It proves intent. Intent matters, but intent alone is not the attempted crime.
Gold Key: Attempt needs intent plus conduct beyond preparation. A statement of intent supplies only one side.

c3.label: CUT B
c3.text: Arrest legality does not answer attempted-possession guilt. Filter: NOT_RESPONSIVE. Mold: misfit.

c3.label: CALL C
c3.text: Agreement is a different inchoate-crime hook. Gold Key kills it. Filter: NOT_RESPONSIVE. Mold: bait_doctrine.

c3.label: CALL D
c3.text: Intent is only one element-type fact. Gold Key kills it. Filter: NOT_RESPONSIVE. Mold: wrong_element.

c3.label: Residual A
c3.text: It is the only answer aimed at the attempt threshold: not enough steps.

studentScript: Attempt call. Ignore arrest legality. Agreement and intent are not enough. No step yet. Pick A.

A.signal: This is the only answer that speaks to the act threshold in an attempt conviction call.
A.lawyer: Common law attempt requires conduct beyond preparation; MPC substantial step would also likely fail on these facts.

B.signal: The answer talks about how police arrested Barnabas, not whether his conduct was enough for attempt.
B.lawyer: An illegal arrest does not itself establish that the defendant did not commit attempt.

C.signal: The answer proves agreement, which is a neighboring inchoate-crime idea, not the act step for attempt.
C.lawyer: Agreement may matter to conspiracy, but it is neither necessary nor sufficient for common law attempt.

D.signal: The answer proves mental state only. The attempt call still needs the act-step side.
D.lawyer: Common law attempt requires more than an unequivocal expression of intent.

goldKeys.statement: Attempt requires more than criminal desire, talk, or agreement. The defendant must take conduct beyond preparation toward the target crime.
goldKeys.trigger: Attempt prosecution where the stem gives only words, a future meeting, and no conduct toward obtaining the target item.
goldKeys.unlocks: Kills agreement-only and intent-only traps; confirms the no-sufficient-steps residual.
goldKeys.authority: lawyer_confirmation: M.P.C. § 5.01(1)(c); People v. Rizzo dangerous-proximity line.

silverKeys.statement: On an attempt call, sort each answer by what it proves: arrest/procedure, agreement, intent, or act step. The act-step answer is the call-matched lane.
silverKeys.trigger: One answer says illegal arrest, one says agreement, one says intent, one says insufficient steps.
silverKeys.unlocks: Element-ladder answer array in attempt questions.

remediation.title: Attempt: talk is not the step
remediation.signal: Future meeting + no act beyond words
remediation.studentMove: Ask: what did the defendant do after forming the plan?
remediation.tinyRule: No act step, no attempt conviction.
remediation.trap: Agreement and intent feel criminal, but the call asks for attempt.
